real_book_1970s_felt_tip.name: real_book_1970s_felt_tip
real_book_1970s_felt_tip.description: Iconic 1970s Berklee Real Book lead-sheet hand written with a bold chisel-tip felt marker, angled slash noteheads, bouncy wide spacing, and stylized lightning-Z quarter rests.
real_book_1970s_felt_tip.paleography_notes: Modeled on the 1974-1975 Berklee College of Music underground Real Book manuscript tradition (copyists working in the wake of Steve Swallow and Paul Bley charts) and commercial jazz lead-sheet conventions codified in Clint Roemer's The Art of Music Copying (1973). Drawn with a broad chisel-tip felt marker held at a steep ~52 deg angle, producing thick flat horizontal beams, crisp angular diamond/slash noteheads, unadorned minimal clefs, and trademark sharp Z-shaped quarter rests on warm photocopied comb-bound stock.

hollywood_ozalid_vellum.name: hollywood_ozalid_vellum
hollywood_ozalid_vellum.description: Golden-Age Hollywood film-studio copyist hand in opaque broad-nib India ink on pale blue-cream translucent vellum/ozalid stock with oversized legible noteheads and bold barlines.
hollywood_ozalid_vellum.paleography_notes: Based on 1940s-1960s Los Angeles film-scoring music preparation departments (MGM, 20th Century Fox, Warner Bros.) and Clint Roemer's The Art of Music Copying. Studio copyists drafted master parts in waterproof India ink using broad music nibs or Pelikan Graphos pens on translucent onion-skin vellum for diazo (Ozalid) reproduction. Designed for zero-rehearsal sight-reading on the scoring stage: oversized solid oval noteheads, razor-straight pre-printed staves, minimal wobble, crisp non-overshooting barlines, and scraped-vellum corrections leaving virtually no eraser smudge.

broadway_pit_copyist_chisel.name: broadway_pit_copyist_chisel
broadway_pit_copyist_chisel.description: New York Broadway pit-orchestra chisel-nib pen hand with high thick-thin contrast, heavy horizontal beams, slight forward lean, and crisp heavy white-cream manuscript stock.
broadway_pit_copyist_chisel.paleography_notes: Reflects the classic New York Local 802 theatrical copy-house style (Associated Music Copy Services, Emily Grishman / Ken Williams' Music Preparation: A Guide to Music Copying, 1980). Written with an Osmiroid italic/music chisel fountain nib on heavy bright white-cream Aztec manuscript paper for dimly lit orchestra pits. Characterized by dramatic thick-thin nib contrast (low nib_min_ratio), bold teardrop noteheads flicked in a single wrist motion, tall clear stems with a slight confident forward lean, heavy horizontal beaming, and disciplined measure proportioning.

big_band_arranger_pencil.name: big_band_arranger_pencil
big_band_arranger_pencil.description: Studio big-band arranger's 2B dark graphite pencil on a 12-staff buff score pad with textured strokes, frequent eraser smudges, rushed bar endings, and bold slash rests.
big_band_arranger_pencil.paleography_notes: Drawn from American big-band and studio arranger score-sketching practice (Count Basie, Thad Jones, Sammy Nestico, Bill Holman traditions) using a soft 2B wooden or mechanical graphite pencil on 12-staff cream/buff score pads. Exhibits high graphite paper-tooth grain, noticeable stroke dropout and tonal variation, frequent eraser smudges from voicing and reharmonization revisions, energetic slanted slash noteheads, hurried diagonal slash/zig quarter rests, rushed end-of-bar cramming, many blank tacet staves, and heavy margin cues for copyists.

nashville_session_sharpie.name: nashville_session_sharpie
nashville_session_sharpie.description: Modern session musician's fine-point black Sharpie/felt-tip hand on crisp white manuscript paper with uniform thick strokes, slight ink bleed and pooling, and wide informal spacing.
nashville_session_sharpie.paleography_notes: Inspired by contemporary Nashville Music Row and commercial tracking-session rhythm/horn charts written rapidly in fine-point black permanent felt-tip marker (Sharpie Fine Point / Sanford) on bright white laser-printed manuscript stock. The round porous tip produces a nearly uniform thick stroke (high nib_min_ratio) with characteristic endpoint ink pooling and modest paper bleed-through, zero erasures, casual compact noteheads, overshooting barlines, bare-bones clefs, and generous form/kicks margin annotations.
